rows.performance_measure_name: % total debt to Council debt limit
rows.story_behind_the_number: Our total debt to Council debt limit is forecast at 46 per cent for 2026.  The forecast decreased from Q1 due to lower self-supported utility debt (excluding ENMAX), which increased The City's borrowing capacity.

rows.performance_measure_name: City of Calgary credit rating (Standard & Poor's 'S&P rating')
Financial stability ratio (fiscal stability reserve %)
rows.story_behind_the_number: In Q2, our financial stability ratio was 9.0 per cent, which is within The City's target range of 5 to 15 per cent. This ratio measures the balance of our Financial Reserve relative to operating, tax-supported gross expenses (net of recoveries), helping ensure we have sufficient reserves to manage financial risks and unexpected costs.

rows.performance_measure_name: Business license applications that have been submitted and completed online - Ease of Service (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: The number remains consistent at 67% in Q2 and continues to show steady progress toward the 80% target. More Calgarians are choosing to apply for business licences online, supported by clearer website content, improved application guidance, and responsive support from the Business Licensing team. Continue enhancing online services and application support to encourage greater adoption of the online application process and increase the percentage of business licence applications submitted and completed online.

rows.performance_measure_name: 311 Telephone Service Factor (% of calls answered in 60 seconds or less)
rows.story_behind_the_number: As forecasted, Telephone Service Factor declined from 93.7% in Q1 to 80% in Q2 due to higher seasonal volumes. Metric still performing at target for Q2. Telephone Service Factor is expected to improve as we complete 311's traditional busy season in Q3.

rows.performance_measure_name: Trust in The City of Calgary (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: From the Q1 Spring Survey of Calgarians, just over one-half (54%) of Calgarians report they trust The City. Due to changes in the spring survey questionnaire, results cannot be directly compared with previous survey waves; however, levels of trust are directionally on par with spring 2025 (52%) and higher than spring 2024 (38%).  The size of the neutral segment is notable, suggesting that a meaningful portion of residents neither firmly trust nor actively distrust The City, but may be undecided or disengaged. This “middle ground” continues to represent an opportunity for The City to strengthen trust through visible actions related to transparency, service performance, and responsiveness.

rows.performance_measure_name: % of Calgarians satisfied with overall City services
rows.story_behind_the_number: Calgarians are surveyed twice annually, in the Spring (Q1) and Fall (Q3). As no new survey results are available for Q2, the Q2 reporting period continues to use the most recent available data from the Q1 2026 Spring Survey. Satisfaction is closely tied to value for tax dollars, with each reinforcing the other. There is a strong connection between service satisfaction and quality of life, reflecting how services shape daily experience. Accessibility and the removal of barriers remain critical drivers, underscoring fairness and reliability in how services are assessed. Updated satisfaction results will be available following the Fall (Q3) survey.

rows.performance_measure_name: Facility Management Assets in Poor & Very Poor Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Over the last few years, we’ve managed to sustain this indicator below the target through strategic investments, interventions, and preventative maintenance activities. However, this indicator remains highly variable due to ongoing data refinement and buildings that are returned to The City, usually in poor condition. Aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance can also contribute to an increase in this performance indicator. Without sufficient investment and early intervention, these assets are at a higher risk of failure, which may impact the services being delivered out of these buildings.

rows.performance_measure_name: Paved roadways in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: One-time capital injection in 2026 will help slow the rate of pavement degradation. Program funding is targeting the backlog of roads in poor condition.

rows.performance_measure_name: Cumulative lane-kilometres of road repaved
rows.story_behind_the_number: The 2026 pavement rehabilitation program has already completed major works in the Edgemont community. Major projects underway include 36th St NE, 32 Ave NE, 90 Ave SW Heritage Dr SW, Bonaventure Dr SE, John Laurie Bv, Country Hills Bv NE, and Shaganappi Tr NW.

rows.performance_measure_name: Sidewalks in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: In response to the Supercharge Sidewalk Remediation Notice of Motion, Council directed Administration to allocate $2.4M from the Fiscal Stability Reserve to fund the remediation of poor sidewalks next to poor condition poplar trees. 50% of the identified locations are scheduled for replacement in 2026.

rows.performance_measure_name: Pathways in Good & Very Good Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Inspections for the pathway network will be completed by the end of August, so the percentage will remain the same until the updated values are reported.

rows.performance_measure_name: Park Assets in Poor & Very Poor Condition (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: From 2023–2026, Parks & Open Spaces directed capital funding toward maintaining and replacing aging park assets. This investment helped meet the 2026 target of keeping assets in Poor and Very Poor condition below 22 per cent, achieving a rate of 18 per cent. Continued investment is needed, as many assets currently in Fair condition are expected to decline over the next five to ten years.

rows.performance_measure_name: Cumulative number of repaired potholes (Year-to-Date)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Maintenance crews have completed more year-to-date pothole repairs than in 2025 due to additional pothole crews being added to night shift operations and additional contractor support.

rows.performance_measure_name: Cumulative kilometres of concrete sidewalk repairs completed
rows.story_behind_the_number: The 2026 concrete rehabilitation program is making good progress with 1261 unique concrete repairs completed in Q2.

rows.performance_measure_name: Snow and ice control completion on priority 1 & 2 routes within targeted timeframes (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Winter maintenance performance targets remained at 100% for the Q2 period which included six total April snow events.

rows.performance_measure_name: Snow and ice control completion on pedestrian infrastructure within targeted timeframes (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: A high level of contractor compliance was achieved through the course of the 2025/26 winter maintenance season.

rows.performance_measure_name: Properties impacted by water outages per 1,000 properties
rows.story_behind_the_number: In 2026, investment in water main replacement continues to increase, with a strategic focus on renewing aging infrastructure and expanding field resources to strengthen preventative maintenance efforts. These investments are designed to improve system reliability, reduce the frequency and impact of water outages, and enhance service delivery for Calgarians. As replacement activities progress and more aging water mains are renewed, outage impacts are expected to stabilize and gradually decline over time.

rows.performance_measure_name: Initial 9-1-1 calls answered within 15 seconds (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: The Alberta 911 Standard (95%) continues to be exceeded. The small decrease between Q1 and Q2 2026 was also observed in 2025 and is typical due to seasonal call volumes that increase in warmer months. The heaviest quarters of call volumes to 9-1-1 are still to come, however, Calgary 9-1-1 is well positioned to meet the standard. Ongoing operational investment for the next budget cycle is essential to maintain critical service delivery, including continuing to meet the call answer standard.

rows.performance_measure_name: % of responses to serious and escalating fires (where two engines, one aerial unit, and a minimum of 12 fire fighters arrived) within 11 minutes (cumulative)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Responses to serious and escalating fires arrived within 11 minutes 75 per cent of the time, up slightly from a year earlier. Results reflected increased aerial staffing and deployment of the first Coverage Engine to support peak demand periods. Continued population growth and densification are increasing service demands. While additional coverage engines and upstaffed aerials in Q3 are expected to maintain improvements, investment over the next budget cycle is essential.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of responses to encampment sites
rows.story_behind_the_number: Responses to encampments typically follow a seasonal pattern. In Q1, with colder weather there are fewer responses, and as temperatures rise in Q2, the number of responses to encampments increases. Responding to encampments highlights the ongoing needs of vulnerable populations in Calgary. Officers continue to focus on outreach and a collaborative approach with Calgary Police Service and Transit Public Safety.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of applications processed for the Fair Entry program
rows.story_behind_the_number: The number of applications processed remain stable as stronger employment rates reduce demand, while complexity of clients’ needs and ongoing accessibility improvements continue to drive the program. Fair Entry launched a new partnership with GreenShield to help eligible clients access essential prescription medications at no cost. It aligns with Fair Entry's purpose of connecting Calgarians to supports that make a meaningful difference in their daily lives.

rows.performance_measure_name: Total number of transit trips (Calgary Transit ridership) (millions)
rows.story_behind_the_number: The decline in ridership compared to Q2 2025 is linked to snow events in April and rainy days in June. On those days, a notable decrease was recorded from the automated passenger counters. Demographic shifts in Calgary may also impact the total number of transit trips. Transit continues to work towards improving service to attract more customers.

rows.performance_measure_name: Trips that arrive within a specified period (%) (i.e. bus on-time performance)
rows.story_behind_the_number: On-time performance slightly decreased between Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. There were weather events in April and May that contributed to a lower on-time performance. Moving forward, changes are coming to a number of bus routes from the outcome of three Transit Service Review projects that included customer feedback. These route improvements begin on August 31.

rows.performance_measure_name: Customer safety rating rate on Transit (%)
rows.story_behind_the_number: Feeling safe on Calgary Transit saw a slight increase of less than one per cent between Q1 and Q2, and remains consistent at 74 per cent. Transit safety continues to increase their presence at CTrain stations through its pilot program. More programs and initiatives are underway with Transit Peace Officers and CPS to improve transit safety. This includes a $9 million Safety Pilot with security staff and dedicated transit peace officers at select stations.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new market homes with development permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 3,277 market homes approved through development permits in Q2 2026, representing a 23% decrease from the previous quarter and a 42% decline year over year. The decline in year over year development permit is consistent with the moderating housing market conditions that were seen in Q1.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new market homes with building permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 6,416 market homes approved through building permits in Q2 2026, representing a 32% increase from the previous quarter and a 5% decrease year over year. Though a small year over year decline is observed, the quarterly increase in building permit approvals indicate that projects are continuing to advance through the development pipeline and moving into the construction phase.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new non-market homes with development permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 112 non-market homes approved through development permits in Q2 2026, representing a 90% increase from the previous quarter and a 61% decrease compared to Q2 2025. Similar to the projections for market homes, we are also seeing a slowdown in non-market housing activity compared to 2025.

rows.performance_measure_name: Number of new non-market homes with building permit approval
rows.story_behind_the_number: There were 84 non-market homes approved through building permits in Q2 2026, representing a 15% decrease from the previous quarter and a 33% decline year over year. However, a high number of development and building permit approvals in 2025 suggest that many non-market homes are in the development pipeline.

rows.performance_measure_name: Total new housing units granted occupancy
rows.story_behind_the_number:
In Q2 2026, the number of homes completed and ready for occupancy remained relatively strong. Although completions were down 65% year-over-year, 2026 is still on track to exceed levels recorded in both 2022 and 2023.
Year-to-date, multi-residential units and townhomes have increased as a share of total housing stock, while semi-detached housing, secondary suites, and detached housing have declined on a proportional basis.

rows.performance_measure_name: New housing units completed in Calgary's Downtown through the conversion of office properties
rows.story_behind_the_number: Completion of projects approved through the Downtown Calgary Office Conversion Program. To date, 793 homes were delivered, of which 170 are non-market. Completion of projects approved through the Downtown Calgary Office Conversion Program. To date, 793 homes were delivered, of which 170 are non-market.
